questions.q: From whom does David need Yahweh to rescue him?
questions.a: David needs Yahweh to rescue him from evil people and protect him from violent people.

questions.q: What does David say about the wicked?
questions.a: David says they say things to people that hurt them and are as deadly as the venom of a viper.

questions.q: What do the violent men plan to do to David?
questions.a: They have planned to destroy him.

questions.q: What have proud people tried to do to David?
questions.a: They are trying to destroy him as though they had hidden traps to catch him.

questions.q: To what does David ask Yahweh to listen?
questions.a: David asks Yahweh to listen to him as he pleads for his help.

questions.q: What did Yahweh do for David during battles?
questions.a: Yahweh powerfully saved David and protected him during battles.

questions.q: What does David want to happen to the leaders who surround him?
questions.a: David wants the harmful things that they have said to others to happen to them.

questions.q: What does David want to happen to those who slander others?
questions.a: David wants anyone who slanders others to have evil things happen to them.

questions.q: What does David know Yahweh will do for the poor and the needy?
questions.a: David knows that Yahweh will do what is just and right for poor people.

questions.q: What will the righteous people surely do?
questions.a: The righteous people will surely give thanks to Yahweh.

questions.q: What will happen to the upright people?
questions.a: They will live in Yahweh’s presence.

commentary.text: He prays for, and prophesies the destruction of, his persecutors.

Verses 1–7 The more danger appears, the more earnest we should be in prayer to God. All are safe whom the Lord protects. If he be for us, who can be against us? We should especially watch and pray, that the Lord would hold up our goings in his ways, that our footsteps slip not. God is as able to keep his people from secret fraud as from open force; and the experience we have had of his power and care, in dangers of one kind, may encourage us to depend upon him in other dangers.

Believers may pray that God would not grant the desires of the wicked, nor further their evil devices. False accusers will bring mischief upon themselves, even the burning coals of Divine vengeance. And surely the righteous shall dwell in God's presence, and give him thanks for evermore. This is true thanksgiving, even thanks-living: this use we should make of all our deliverances, we should serve God the more closely and cheerfully. Those who, though evil spoken of and ill-used by men, are righteous in the sight of God, being justified by the righteousness of Christ, which is imputed to them, and received by faith, as the effect of which, they live soberly and righteously; these give thanks to the Lord, for the righteousness whereby they are made righteous, and for every blessing of grace, and mercy of life.
